sections.heading: The legal rule
Essential ingredients
Definitions and key terms
sections.body:
“act” — as well a series of acts as a single act.
“animal” — any living creature, other than a human being.
“child” — any person below the age of eighteen years.
“Court” — a Judge who is empowered by law to act judicially alone, or a body of Judges which is empowered by law to act judicially as a body, when such Judge or body of Judges is acting judicially.
“death” — the death of a human being unless the contrary appears from the context.
“dishonestly” — doing anything with the intention of causing wrongful gain to one person or wrongful loss to another person.
“document” — any matter expressed or described upon any substance by means of letters, figures or marks, or by more than one of those means, and includes electronic and digital record, intended to be used, or which may be used, as evidence of that matter Explanation 1.—It is immaterial by what means or upon what substance the letters, figures or marks are formed, or whether the evidence is intended for, or may be used in a Court or not Illustrations (a) A writing expressing the terms of a contract, which may be used as evidence of the contract, is a document (b) A cheque upon a banker is a document (c) A power-of-attorney is a document (d) A map or plan which is intended to be used or which may be used as evidence, is a document (e) A writing containing directions or instructions is a document Explanation 2.—Whatever is expressed by means of letters, figures or marks as explained by mercantile or other usage, shall be deemed to be expressed by such letters, figures or marks within the meaning of this section, although the same may not be actually expressed Illustration A writes his name on the back of a bill of exchange payable to his order.
“fraudulently” — doing anything with the intention to defraud but not otherwise.
“Government” — the Central Government or a State Government.
“harbour” — supplying a person with shelter, food, drink, money, clothes, arms, ammunition or means of conveyance, or the assisting a person by any means, whether of the same kind as those enumerated in this clause or not, to evade apprehension.
“injury” — any harm whatever illegally caused to any person, in body, mind, reputation or property.
“Judge” — a person who is officially designated as a Judge and includes a person,– (i) who is empowered by law to give, in any legal proceeding, civil or criminal, a definitive judgment, or a judgment which, if not appealed against, would be definitive, or a judgment which, if confirmed by some other authority, would be definitive.
“life” — the life of a human being, unless the contrary appears from the context.
“local law” — a law applicable only to a particular part of India.
“man” — male human being of any age.
“movable property” — property of every description, except land and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything which is attached to the earth.
“oath” — a solemn affirmation substituted by law for an oath, and any declaration required or authorised by law to be made before a public servant or to be used for the purpose of proof, whether in a Court or not.
“offence” — a thing made punishable by this Sanhita, but–– (a) in Chapter III and in the following sections, namely, sub-sections (2), (3), (4) and (5) of section 8, sections 9, 49, 50, 52, 54, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61, 119, 120, 123, sub-sections (7) and (8) of section 127, 222, 230, 231, 240, 248, 250, 251, 259, 260, 261, 262, 263, sub-sections (6) and (7) of section 308 and sub-section (2) of section 330, the word “offence” means a thing punishable under this Sanhita, or under any special law or local law.
“omission” — as well as a series of omissions as a single omission.
“person” — any company or association or body of persons, whether incorporated or not.
“public” — any class of the public or any community.
“public servant” — a person falling under any of the descriptions, namely:— (a) every commissioned officer in the Army, Navy or Air Force.
“election” — an election for the purpose of selecting members of any legislative, municipal or other public authority, of whatever character, the method of selection to which is by, or under any law for the time being in force Illustration A Municipal Commissioner is a public servant.
“special law” — a law applicable to a particular subject.
“valuable security” — a document which is, or purports to be, a document whereby any legal right is created, extended, transferred, restricted, extinguished or released, or whereby any person acknowledges that he lies under legal liability, or has not a certain legal right Illustration A writes his name on the back of a bill of exchange.
“vessel” — anything made for the conveyance by water of human beings or of property.
“will” — any testamentary document.
“woman” — a female human being of any age.
“wrongful gain” — gain by unlawful means of property to which the person gaining is not legally entitled.
“wrongful loss” — the loss by unlawful means of property to which the person losing it is legally entitled.

examples.title: Illustration (f)
examples.body:
A writes his name on the back of a bill of exchange payable to his order. The meaning of the endorsement, as explained by mercantile usage, is that the bill is to be paid to the holder. The endorsement is a document, and shall be construed in the same manner as if the words “pay to the holder” or words to that effect had been written over the signature;

What it teaches: this is an official illustration printed in the section. In the answer, map it to an ingredient of BNS s. 2 — which fact proves which element, and what the legal result is.

examples.title: Illustration (g)
examples.body:
A Magistrate exercising jurisdiction in respect of a charge on which he has power to sentence to fine or imprisonment, with or without appeal, is a Judge;

What it teaches: this is an official illustration printed in the section. In the answer, map it to an ingredient of BNS s. 2 — which fact proves which element, and what the legal result is.

examples.title: Illustration (h)
examples.body:
A Municipal Commissioner is a public servant;

What it teaches: this is an official illustration printed in the section. In the answer, map it to an ingredient of BNS s. 2 — which fact proves which element, and what the legal result is.

examples.title: Illustration (i)
examples.body:
A writes his name on the back of a bill of exchange. As the effect of this endorsement is to transfer the right to the bill to any person who may become the lawful holder of it, the endorsement is a “valuable security”;

What it teaches: this is an official illustration printed in the section. In the answer, map it to an ingredient of BNS s. 2 — which fact proves which element, and what the legal result is.

examples.title: Illustration (j)
examples.body:
A sets fire, by night, to an inhabited house in a large town, for the purpose of facilitating a robbery and thus causes the death of a person. Here, A may not have intended to cause death; and may even be sorry that death has been caused by his act; yet, if he knew that he was likely to cause death, he has caused death voluntarily;

What it teaches: this is an official illustration printed in the section. In the answer, map it to an ingredient of BNS s. 2 — which fact proves which element, and what the legal result is.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Legal Assessment & Statutory Note: BNS s. 2 (Definitions)
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. BNS s. 2 deals with Definitions. It sits in Chapter I — Preliminary of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Section 2 is the dictionary. IPC definitions that were scattered across ss. 6–52 now sit here. The headline addition: “child” means any person below eighteen years.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 2 is the rule on “Definitions”. The section provides that in this Sanhita, unless the context otherwise requires, ––. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. In this Sanhita, unless the context otherwise requires, ––
2. (1) “act” denotes as well a series of acts as a single act;
3. (2) “animal” means any living creature, other than a human being;
4. (3) “child” means any person below the age of eighteen years;
5. (4) “counterfeit”.–A person is said to “counterfeit” who causes one thing to resemble another thing, intending by means of that resemblance to practise deception, or knowing it to be likely that deception will thereby be practised
6. (9) “fraudulently” means doing anything with the intention to defraud but not otherwise;
7. (10) “gender”. —The pronoun “he” and its derivatives are used of any person, whether male, female or transgender
8. (17) “life” means the life of a human being, unless the contrary appears from the context;

Definitions. The core statutory definitions must be established:
“act” as well a series of acts as a single act. “animal” any living creature, other than a human being. “child” any person below the age of eighteen years. “Court” a Judge who is empowered by law to act judicially alone, or a body of Judges which is empowered by law to act judicially as a body, when such Judge or body of Judges is acting judicially. “death” the death of a human being unless the contrary appears from the context. “dishonestly” doing anything with the intention of causing wrongful gain to one person or wrongful loss to another person. “document” any matter expressed or described upon any substance by means of letters, figures or marks, or by more than one of those means, and includes electronic and digital record, intended to be used, or which may be used, as evidence of that matter Explanation 1.—It is immaterial by what means or upon what substance the letters, figures or marks are formed, or whether the evidence is intended for, or may be used in a Court or not Illustrations (a) A writing expressing the terms of a contract, which may be used as evidence of the contract, is a document (b) A cheque upon a banker is a document (c) A power-of-attorney is a document (d) A map or plan which is intended to be used or which may be used as evidence, is a document (e) A writing containing directions or instructions is a document Explanation 2.—Whatever is expressed by means of letters, figures or marks as explained by mercantile or other usage, shall be deemed to be expressed by such letters, figures or marks within the meaning of this section, although the same may not be actually expressed Illustration A writes his name on the back of a bill of exchange payable to his order. “fraudulently” doing anything with the intention to defraud but not otherwise.

Illustrations. The section itself supplies worked examples. In legal analysis, pick one illustration, restate its facts, and show which ingredient it proves. Illustration (a): (a) A writing expressing the terms of a contract, which may be used as evidence of the contract, is a document

Explanations. Explanation 1.—It is not essential to counterfeiting that the imitation should be exact An explanation is not optional commentary. It is part of the section and must appear in an authoritative brief.

Limitations. Apply only the conditions written in s. 2. Do not import a defence from a different chapter unless the question requires it.

Conclusion. BNS s. 2 is the complete current-law heading for Definitions. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Complete statutory structure: introduction, meaning, ingredients, illustration, explanation/exception, application, and current-law citation.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Name, commencement, extra-territorial reach, the dictionary, and how the Sanhita is read — including common intention in s. 3(5).. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 3 — Analytical comment. Explain a condition, a proviso, or a practical difficulty in applying s. 2. Do not invent case names.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 2.”

cases.name: Independent Thought v. Union of India
cases.holding: The marital-rape exception cannot apply to a wife under 18. The exception in s. 63 must be read with this holding and the POCSO overlap.

examTips: Cite BNS s. 2 for offences on or after 1 July 2024.
Ingredients first, illustration second, application third, conclusion last.

revisionPoints: First ingredient: In this Sanhita, unless the context otherwise requires, ––

For offences on or after 1 July 2024, the correct citation is BNS s. 2 — Definitions. Older books and judgments may still print a historical number (6–52 (definitions relocated)). Convert it. Write the BNS number in a current answer. Do not treat the old number as if it were still the law.
content.migrationNote: Imported from the codepackr-law legacy topic catalog. Status is review until authoritative provenance and current-law verification are completed.

learningObjectives: Explain why BNS s.2 functions as the statutory dictionary.
Identify definitions that materially affect criminal liability.
Apply a defined term to facts without importing a different statutory meaning.
enhancement.definition: BNS s.2 supplies defined meanings for recurring expressions used in the Sanhita, subject to the statutory qualification that the context may require otherwise.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A statutory definition controls interpretation within its statutory field unless the provision itself permits contextual departure. A strong exam answer identifies the exact defined expression and then applies its elements to the facts.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: BNS s.2 public-servant descriptions (a)-(k) now checked against India Code. Section not marked verified.
essentialIngredients: Quote or accurately paraphrase only the portion relevant to the issue.
Check any statutory exceptions, explanations or special clauses attached to that definition.
Apply each definitional element to the facts.
Check whether another statute is incorporated by the cross-reference in s.2(39).
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 2 is not merely a list to memorise. Its definitions operate as building blocks for later offences. For example, whether conduct involves a 'document', whether a person is a 'public servant', whether a gain is 'wrongful', or whether an act was done 'voluntarily' can change the analysis of a substantive offence. In an answer, start with the definition and then demonstrate the factual match element by element.
examples: If a question turns on whether an electronic record can fall within 'document', analyse the statutory wording concerning electronic and digital records rather than relying on ordinary-language meaning.
For 'child', apply the statutory age threshold stated in s.2.
For 'wrongful gain' or 'wrongful loss', identify the unlawful means and the relevant property entitlement.
For 'reason to believe', ask whether the facts disclose the sufficient cause required by the definition.

rows.left: BNS statutory wording controls within its scope.
rows.right: Ordinary meaning is not a substitute where Parliament has defined the term.

rows.left: Break the definition into elements and apply facts.
rows.right: Use ordinary meaning only where the statute leaves room for it.

enhancement.problemApplication: When a problem turns on a definition, identify the disputed word first. Then reproduce its statutory components, match each fact to each component, and explain any contextual qualification. Do not jump directly from the facts to the offence conclusion.

examAnswerStructure.shortAnswer: State the definition, identify its two or three most relevant elements, and apply them to the fact.
examAnswerStructure.tenMark: Introduction → purpose of statutory definitions → relevant definition → elements → factual application → connected offence → conclusion.
examAnswerStructure.sixteenMark: Introduction → interpretive role of s.2 → detailed definition and exceptions/cross-references → competing factual interpretations → application to the substantive offence → conclusion.

keyTakeaways: Section 2 is a statutory dictionary, not a standalone offence.
Use the exact defined term relevant to the question.
Definitions must be applied element by element.

notes: In-progress enhancement. Verify the complete current definition list before publication.

Official marginal heading checked: s.2 Definitions. Source: India Code bitstream 123456789/20062, BNS Act 45 of 2023, arrangement of sections, text as on 6 October 2025. Heading only. Body not re-read.

Body check 2026-10-03: India Code bitstream 123456789/20062, text as on 6 October 2025. Heading Definitions confirmed. Clauses read: (1) act includes a series of acts; (2) animal means any living creature other than a human being; (3) child means a person below eighteen; (5) Court; (6) death means death of a human being unless context shows otherwise; (7) dishonestly means intention of causing wrongful gain to one person or wrongful loss to another; (8) document includes electronic and digital record; (9) fraudulently means intention to defraud but not otherwise; (10) gender pronoun he includes male, female or transgender, with transgender defined by the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 s.2(k). Later clauses, including counterfeit, were not re-read. Status remains in-progress.

Further body check 2026-10-03, same India Code PDF. Clause (4) counterfeit read with both explanations: exact imitation is not essential; a deceiving resemblance presumes intention or knowledge until the contrary is proved. Also read (11) good faith requires due care and attention; (12) Government means Central or State Government; (13) harbour; (14) injury; (15) illegal and legally bound to do; (17) life; (18) local law; (19) man; (20) month and year by the Gregorian calendar; (21) movable property; (22) number; (23) oath; (24) offence, including the special-law and local-law extensions. Clause (16) and clauses after (24) were not in the extracts read. Status remains in-progress.

Further body check 2026-10-03, same India Code PDF. Clause (16) Judge read, including the Magistrate illustration. Also read (28) public servant opening clauses (a) and (b) and the two explanations that appointment by Government is unnecessary and a defect in title does not prevent a person in actual possession of the situation from being a public servant; the remaining public-servant descriptions were not extracted. Also read (29) reason to believe; (30) special law; (31) valuable security; (33) voluntarily; (34) will; (35) woman; (36) wrongful gain; (37) wrongful loss; (38) gaining wrongfully and losing wrongfully, through the sentence that gaining includes retaining and losing includes being kept out. Clauses (25)-(27) and (32) were not in the extracts read. Status remains in-progress.

Further body check 2026-10-03, same India Code PDF. Clause (25) omission includes a series of omissions. (26) person includes a company or association or body of persons, whether incorporated or not. (27) public includes any class of the public or any community. (32) vessel means anything made for the conveyance by water of human beings or of property. (39) undefined words take their meaning from the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. Public servant descriptions read: (c) officer of a Court, including liquidator, receiver or commissioner, and a person specially authorised by a Court; (d) assessor or member of a panchayat assisting a Court or public servant; (g) Government officer whose duty is to prevent offences, give information, bring offenders to justice, or protect public health, safety or convenience; (h) officer who takes, receives, keeps or expends property, or surveys, assesses, contracts, executes a revenue-process, or protects the pecuniary interests of the Government. Descriptions (e) and (f) were not in the extract. Status remains in-progress.

Further body check 2026-10-03, same India Code PDF. Public servant (e): every arbitrator or other person to whom any cause or matter has been referred for decision or report by any Court, or by any other competent public authority. (f): every person who holds any office by virtue of which he is empowered to place or keep any person in confinement. The same extract also showed (j) a person empowered to prepare, publish, maintain or revise an electoral roll or to conduct an election or part of an election, and the opening of (k) a person in the service or pay of the Government or remunerated by fees or commission for a public duty. Description (i) and the remainder of (k) were not extracted. Status remains in-progress.

Further body check 2026-10-03, same India Code PDF. Public servant (i): every officer whose duty is to take, receive, keep or expend property, make a survey or assessment, or levy a rate or tax for any secular common purpose of any village, town or district, or to make, authenticate or keep a document for ascertaining the rights of the people of any village, town or district. (k): a person in the service or pay of the Government or remunerated by fees or commission for a public duty by the Government; and a person in the service or pay of a local authority as defined in the General Clauses Act, 1897 s.3(31), a corporation established by or under a Central or State Act, or a Government company as defined in the Companies Act, 2013 s.2(45). Explanation (c): election means an election for selecting members of any legislative, municipal or other public authority, the method of selection being by or under any law in force. Status of the whole section remains in-progress because the topic was not promoted.
